top_story: Israel’s security anxieties sharpened on 30 September after an Israel-bound Flydubai flight from the UAE was forced down in Saudi Arabia when a pilot allegedly stabbed his co-pilot and may have tried to crash the aircraft, extending the sense of threat beyond Gaza and Israel’s borders into regional transit routes. That same day, Israeli attacks in Gaza killed eight people, including a journalist, pushing the toll among Palestinian media workers since October 2023 to 263 and reinforcing how routine violence continues to erase civilian and reporting capacity alike. The deadliest development came hours later in Iran, where the bombing of a school in Minab killed 120 children and turned a civilian sanctuary into a mass grave, a strike likely to deepen public fury and harden perceptions of a widening U.S.-Israeli war on civilians. The regional picture is one of conflict spilling across airspace, borders, and civilian institutions, with fear, grief, and political radicalization feeding each other.
